- per-tenant policy CRD
- bidirectional gRPC capability negotiation

- canary-friendly rollout and end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD blueprint (high level)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnffeaturepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenantID:
                  type: string
                features:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: string

  names:
    plural: cnffeaturepolicies
    singular: cnffeaturepolicy
    kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
    shortNames: [cfp]
```

```yaml

apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: CNFFeaturePolicy

  name: tenant-a-policy

    - QUIC
    - TLS13
    - multiplexing
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement tenant-scoped feature gating, combining CRDs, policy-as-code, and canary-style risk mitigation in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- FeatureGate CRD and TenantFeatureGate per-tenant
- OPA Gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Path-based canary gating and per-tenant isolation
- Minimal YAML for CRD, policy, namespace, and a basic test

## Code Example
```yaml
# FeatureGate CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featuregates.example.org
spec:
  group: example.org
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featuregates
    singular: featuregate
    kind: FeatureGate
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (OPA)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sfeaturegate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sFeatureGate
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sfeaturegate
        violation["deny"] {
          input.target.path == "/v1/beta"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["tenant/feature-v1-beta"] == "enabled"
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-tenant)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sFeatureGate
metadata:
  name: tenant-v1beta-enabled
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["gateway.example.org"]
        kinds: ["GatewayRoute"]
  parameters:
    # feature flag key used in tenant annotation
    flagKey: "tenant/feature-v1-beta"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest enabling the flag
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    tenant/feature-v1-beta: enabled
```

```bash
# quick test (pseudo)
curl -H "Host: gateway.example.org" https://gateway/health
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world per-tenant canary strategies, traffic splitting, and rollback logic under latency and error constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Canary rollout with per-tenant isolation
- Prometheus metric-driven analysis
- Rollout/VirtualService integration

  name: gateway-rollout

  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/org/gateway:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 900s }
      - setWeight: 100

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime attestation bridging CI and runtime, using SPIFFE/mTLS, OPA, and per-tenant revocation. Evaluates trade-offs around performance, key management, and revocation latency.

## Key Concepts

- Runtime attestation evidence (image digest, SBOM hash, runtime state)

- Per-tenant revocation and key rotation for attestations
- Testing in a single namespace before broader rollout

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: attestation-agent
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: example/attestation-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: ATTESTATION_ENDPOINT
          value: https://attestor.default.svc.cluster.local
        - name: CERT_FILE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: attestation-cert
              key: tls.crt
        - name: KEY_FILE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: attestation-cert
              key: tls.key
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle revocation propagation when an attacker signs a new image at runtime?
